Step 2 (General Knowledge): The shared experience of creatinglifelike imitation is a key part of the attraction of animation (p. 21).
Step 3 (General Knowledge): The idea of projecting shadows led to the first magiclantern shows, starting around the mid to late 1700s and lastinguntil the introduction (p. 21).
Step 4 (General Knowledge): A primitive projection devicelike a wooden box with a candle inside was fitted with a lens (p. 21).

pamphlet_excerpts: Principles of Animation: The principles of animation are a set of 12 basic ideas applied toanimation to create appealing, believable results (p. 35).
Principles of Animation Principle 2: They wereintroduced by two of the original Disney animators, Ollie Johnston and Frank Thomas, in their book, Disney Animation: The Illusion (p. 35).
Principles of Animation Principle 3: Since that time, the principles havebecome standard in the animation industry (p. 35).
Principles of Animation Principle 4: Straight Ahead Action and Pose to Pose Straight-ahead action and pose to pose are the two mainmethods for animating (p. 35).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Principles of Animation): Using straight-ahead action, theanimator draws or animates frame by frame, doing the drawingsin order: 1, 2, 3, 4 (p. 35).
Step 2 (Principles of Animation): With pose-to-pose animation, incontrast, the animator draws or poses the main (key) frames of the animation before filling in the in-between (p. 35).
Step 3 (Principles of Animation): Using thepose-to-pose method, the animator might do drawing 1, thendrawing 25, and then drawing 47, before going back to do thedrawings (p. 35).
Step 4 (Principles of Animation): Most animators use the pose-to-pose method becauseit offers benefits in timing and frame composition (p. 35).
